title: Unit 1, Lesson 1: Bangabandhu's Childhood
instruction: Read the passage carefully and answer the questions following it:
passage: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was born in the village of Tungipara under Gopalganj district on 17 March 1920. His father Sheikh Lutfar Rahman was a serestadar in the Gopalganj civil court and his mother was Sayera Khatun. Mujib was the third child among four daughters and two sons. His parents used to call him 'Khoka' affectionately. At the age of seven, in 1927, he was admitted to Gimadanga Primary School. Later he studied at Gopalganj Public School and completed his matriculation from Gopalganj Missionary School in 1942. From his early childhood, Mujib showed a deep sense of empathy for the poor and oppressed people around him. During his school days, he gave away his own umbrella to a poor classmate who was drenched in heavy rain. He also distributed rice from his father's granary to the famine-affected villagers. He was a brave, kind-hearted boy with a natural gift for leadership.
